title: AI Spending Fears Threaten to Swamp Big Tech’s Strong Earnings
summary: Three of the biggest and most important technology companies in the world are expected to show healthy growth when they report earnings this week.

title: Markets Look to Big Tech for AI Payoff
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, MetLife Investment Management Chief Market Strategist Drew Matus examines how AI investment is driving markets, corporate spending and parts of the US economy as investors look to Big Tech earnings for evidence that the spending will pay off. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Matus discusses risks from rising technology investment and what markets need to hear from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on inflation. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Can Mistral Challenge Big Tech by Doing AI Differently?
summary: Europe has fallen behind the US in the race to build the biggest AI models, constrained by smaller capital markets and a fragmented business environment. France-based Mistral is betting it can compete differently using open-source models to offer companies lower costs, more control over their data and greater technological sovereignty. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ray-Ban Meta Audio AI Glasses Cost More While Ditching a Key Feature: Review
summary: Meta Platforms Inc.’s $349-and-up Ray-Ban Meta Audio, announced last month, are an odd proposition. On the one hand, they’re more expensive than some of the company’s entry-level models and yet they do many of the same things:  play music, make calls, answer questions through Meta’s artificial intelligence assistant, or let the wearer dictate texts and audio messages. title: JPMorgan’s Private Bank Using AI to Make Advisers More Efficient
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s private bank is using artificial intelligence to onboard clients, for investment research and other tasks in an effort to increase productivity among its wealth advisers, according to its Europe, Middle East and Africa head, Pablo Garnica.

title: Chinese Manufacturer Dongshan Raises $1.3 Billion in HK Listing
summary: Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co. a printed circuit board maker, raised about HK$9.9 billion ($1.3 billion) in Hong Kong’s biggest listing in nearly two months, which hit a volatile market for companies related to the artificial intelligence build out.

title: Bank of Israel Slams Netanyahu’s Anti-Sanction Crypto Scheme
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu floated using cryptocurrency to get around potential financial sanctions on Israel, prompting a strongly-worded rebuke from the central bank.

title: AI Provides ‘Zero Payoff’ to S&P 493 Outside Tech, Apollo Economist Says
summary: Despite the significant investments ploughed into artificial intelligence it has provided “zero payoff” to corporate America outside of technology, according to Apollo Global Management Inc. Chief Economist Torsten Slok.

title: SoftBank’s Son Plans $50 Billion Malaysia Tech Outlay, PM Says
summary: Masayoshi Son of SoftBank Group Corp. chose locations in Malaysia for $50 billion in technology investments, the country’s prime minister said, an outlay that would accelerate the billionaire’s global bet on AI infrastructure.

title: UAE Shuts More Beaches as It Deals with Oil Spill in Gulf
summary: The United Arab Emirates shut more beaches after an oil spill in the Persian Gulf raised concerns over environmental and health impacts.

title: Australia Police Chief Says Angry Debate Adds Risks to Lawmakers
summary: Acrimonious political debate in Australia is escalating risks to legislators, one of the country’s most senior police officers said after a lawmaker suffered serious injuries following an alleged attack.

title: Sinking Profits Turn China’s $3.5 Trillion Stock Rout Into Trap
summary: Pessimism has gripped Chinese stocks, with no end in sight for a deepening selloff as investors confront the realities of an economy that’s weak enough to erode corporate profits but not to trigger forceful new stimulus.
